headline: High: shared filesystem and broad write/network capabilities create default risks of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors between ChatGPT Desktop and Plandex.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can read files and clipboard/screen content, while Plandex reads and writes the project directory and plan-local sandbox. That creates a plausible content bridge where attacker-controlled text from one can be treated as instructions by the other. This is not fully automatic, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF ChatGPT Desktop ingests a file or clipboard payload originating from Plandex output
IF Plandex reads a file that ChatGPT Desktop previously summarized or edited
mitigations: Keep a separate handoff file for model outputs and mark it untrusted
Disable clipboard-based transfer between the two agents
Require human review before either agent consumes the other's generated text
Use read-only copies for any shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to exchanged files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents can read files, and ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code while Plandex can write the project directory. In a shared workspace, sensitive material can flow from ChatGPT Desktop into Plandex outputs or logs. The profiles do not prove uncontrolled exfiltration, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same project directory or uploaded artifact set
IF ChatGPT Desktop is given screenshots, voice, or connected-IDE code containing sensitive data
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for each agent
Strip secrets from files before handing them to Plandex
Avoid uploading screenshots or voice transcripts containing sensitive data
Review Plandex outputs before saving them back into shared folders
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the OS level

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Plandex has execute_shell, write_filesystem, and modify_git_state, while ChatGPT Desktop can read files and interact with supported macOS apps plus clipboard/screen surfaces. If both touch the same repo or directory, concurrent edits and git-state changes can collide and corrupt work. The shared-state risk is stronger than a mere read overlap, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same git repository or filesystem tree
IF Plandex auto-applies changes while ChatGPT Desktop is also editing or reading the same files
mitigations: Assign only one agent write access to the repo at a time
Turn off auto-apply in Plandex during shared work
Use git branches per agent and merge manually
Pause ChatGPT Desktop file access while Plandex applies changes
requires-engineering: add file-locking or orchestration locks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plandex is a planner that stages changes before apply, but it can still act on ChatGPT Desktop outputs if those outputs are copied into the plan. ChatGPT Desktop can produce code or file-derived summaries that Plandex may treat as authoritative without verification. The review-then-apply flow reduces but does not eliminate this risk.
conditions: IF ChatGPT Desktop-generated text is pasted into a Plandex plan without independent verification
IF Plandex auto-apply is enabled for changes derived from ChatGPT Desktop output
mitigations: Require a second human check before apply
Ask Plandex to cite source files for every proposed change
Compare ChatGPT Desktop summaries against original files manually
Disable auto-apply for plans sourced from another agent
requires-engineering: add structured provenance checks between agents

E_compliance.rationale: The profiles show different data classes and storage models, but no explicit residency or certification mismatch is documented. ChatGPT Desktop handles uploaded files and screenshots; Plandex handles source code and model-provider keys. Without a stated cross-border or regulated-data flow, only a low compliance concern is supportable.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is placed into ChatGPT Desktop and then copied into Plandex
IF organizational policy requires identical retention or residency controls across both tools
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both tools
Use redacted samples for planning and coding
Check vendor retention settings before use
Document which data classes each agent may touch
requires-engineering: obtain a DPA or residency attestation for the full workflow
